question: Through which methods can a Georgia boat owner apply for or renew a vessel registration?
choice_a: Online at GoOutdoorsGeorgia.com, by telephone at 1-800-366-2661, or by mail using a downloaded application submitted to the DNR
choice_b: Only in person at a county tax commissioner's tag office
choice_c: Only through a private boat dealer at the time of purchase
choice_d: Only by mailing a paper form -- there is no phone or online option
explanation: Georgia offers three ways to apply for or renew a vessel registration: online at www.gooutdoorsgeorgia.com, by telephone at 1-800-366-2661 for all boating transactions, or by downloading and mailing/emailing an application via the DNR boating registration page.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'How to Apply For or Renew Your Vessel's Registration'

question: How far in advance of the expiration date is a Georgia boat registration renewal form mailed to the owner?
choice_a: 60 days after the expiration date has already passed
choice_b: At least 30 days before the expiration date
choice_c: On the exact day the registration expires
choice_d: Renewal forms are never mailed to owners
explanation: A renewal form is mailed to the vessel owner at least 30 days prior to the expiration date; it may be returned by mail, or the owner may renew by telephone or online.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'How to Apply For or Renew Your Vessel's Registration'

question: Besides the assigned registration number, what does Georgia require regarding other numbers displayed on the bow of a registered vessel?
choice_a: Owners may add a second, decorative number of their own choosing
choice_b: A second number is required to show the vessel's model year
choice_c: No other numbers may be displayed on either side of the bow besides the registration number
choice_d: Additional numbers are allowed only on personal watercraft
explanation: Along with the display requirements for the registration number itself, Georgia law states that no other numbers may be displayed on either side of the bow.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Registering Your Vessel'

question: How must the letters be separated from the numbers within a displayed Georgia registration number, such as GA 3717 ZW?
choice_b: By a forward slash, e.g., GA/3717/ZW
choice_c: No separation between the letters and numbers is required or permitted
choice_d: By a space or a hyphen, e.g., GA 3717 ZW or GA-3717-ZW
explanation: Georgia requires the letters to be separated from the numbers by a space or a hyphen, for example GA 3717 ZW or GA-3717-ZW.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Registering Your Vessel'

question: Where must the current validation decal be displayed in relation to the registration number on the bow?
choice_a: On each side of the bow, preceding (before) the prefix letters of the registration number
choice_b: On the stern only, never on the bow
choice_c: Anywhere on the vessel -- placement does not matter
choice_d: Only on the port side of the bow, never the starboard side
explanation: Current validation decals must be displayed on each side of the bow, preceding the prefix letters of the registration number.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Registering Your Vessel'

question: If a vessel owner loses or destroys the Certificate of Boat Registration or a validation decal, how do they obtain a duplicate and what is the fee?
choice_a: Nothing can be done -- Georgia does not issue duplicate certificates or decals
choice_b: Apply for a duplicate by renewing the registration and checking the 'duplicate' box on the form; the fee is $1 plus the appropriate transaction fee
choice_d: Re-register the vessel as brand new at the full three-year registration fee
explanation: A lost or destroyed Certificate of Boat Registration or decal is replaced by applying for a duplicate through the renewal process and checking the 'duplicate' box; the fee is $1 plus the appropriate transaction fee.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Other Facts About Registering Your Vessel'

question: What documentation must the buyer of a brand-new vessel have in order to register it in Georgia?
choice_a: Only a verbal confirmation of sale from the dealer
choice_b: A Georgia title transferred from a previous owner
choice_c: The Original Manufacturer's Statement of Origin and the dealer's invoice/bill of sale
choice_d: No documentation is required to register a new vessel
explanation: For a new vessel, the buyer is required to have the Original Manufacturer's Statement of Origin along with the dealer's invoice/bill of sale as proof of a legal ownership trail.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Buying and Selling a Vessel'

question: When buying a used vessel currently registered in another state, what determines whether the buyer needs a transfer title versus just a registration card and bills of sale?
choice_a: Georgia never accepts documentation from any out-of-state vessel under any circumstance
choice_b: Only the buyer's Georgia driver's license matters, regardless of the seller's state
choice_c: No documentation beyond the seller's spoken word is ever required
choice_d: Whether the seller's state requires titles: a Transfer Title is needed if coming from a title state, while a current registration card plus all bills of sale suffice if coming from a non-title state
explanation: For a used vessel registered in another state, the buyer needs a Transfer Title if coming from a state that requires titles, or a current registration card plus all bills of sale from the last owner of record if not coming from a title state.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Buying and Selling a Vessel'

question: What happens if an application to transfer ownership of a vessel remains incomplete for more than 60 days?
choice_a: It must be resubmitted along with a new application fee
choice_b: DNR automatically completes it using whatever information is on file
choice_c: The vessel's registration is permanently canceled with no option to resubmit
choice_d: Nothing -- there is no time limit on completing a transfer application
explanation: Ownership-transfer applications that remain incomplete after 60 days must be resubmitted along with a new application fee.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Buying and Selling a Vessel'

question: A 14-foot sailboat with no motor is operated on Georgia's public waters. Must it be registered?
choice_a: No, sailboats of any length are always exempt from registration
choice_b: Yes -- only sailboats UNDER 12 feet in length (with no mechanical propulsion) are exempt from Georgia's registration requirement, so a 14-foot sailboat must be registered
choice_c: No, sailboats are exempt from registration up to 20 feet in length
choice_d: Registration is optional for any sailboat under 30 feet
explanation: Georgia's registration exemption applies only to sailboats under 12 feet in length with no mechanical propulsion; a 14-foot sailboat exceeds that threshold and must be registered like other covered vessels.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Registering Your Vessel'

question: A vessel is currently and validly registered in another state. For how long may it be operated on Georgia's public waters before Georgia registration becomes required?
choice_d: It may never be operated in Georgia without first obtaining Georgia registration
explanation: Vessels registered in other states are exempt from Georgia registration while using Georgia waters for 60 days or less; beyond that, Georgia registration is required.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Registering Your Vessel'
